title: Glenn Miller's offer in 1939 and the Maurice Purtle hire
summary: Asked about leaving the business, Leeman says he was too weak after illness in May 1939, and Glenn Miller hired Maurice Purtle instead.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing in Lionel Hampton's big band

blocks.x: I've seen in some of the jazz magazines and some of the jazz histories that you left the business for two years, from 1945 to 1947 -- is that so?
Well, you've skipped the main years of my life, as growing up in the big bands.
From Artie Shaw -- well, I got these calls from Glenn Miller and I started to say -- would I like to come with his band. Well, I hadn't learned to walk properly after being in bed for so long.
This was Spring -- May and June of '39.

Because this was when -- I wasn't ready, I talked to Glenn, and he said, 'Well, we're opening the at old Orchard Beach Glen Island Casino, so if we play a one nighter, we'll watch you' -- and I said 'Well, I'll be ready to play and I'll come out to see you.'
Well, I went out there, and he had hired Maurice Purtle to play drums, they had put him under contract -- he said he couldn't wait.
Yeah, we called him Moe Purtle.
